race: Formula 1 Gran Premio de la Ciudad de México 2026

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Welcome to The Race Weekend Podcast, and Mexico City is about to get proper spicy this weekend, with the title hanging over everything.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Kimi Antonelli is missing Thursday media day with an illness, but he just won the US GP and the title is still in play, so the story is huge.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is the story, is the champion in waiting still enough to clinch it before the season ends, or does the weekend decide it?

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: There is even a big question now, how much of Antonelli's success is down to his ability, and the answer is still up for debate.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: And F1 has floated simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s for the next rules, so the sport is already looking ahead while the title fight is live.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Also, after the last race, Antonelli was superb and Leclerc was close to perfect, so the fight is real and the pace is scary.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Okay, top three, let's start with Kimi Antonelli, championship leader, nine wins, and a Mercedes that is hard to move all weekend.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: I know the Mexico history is average sixth, but when the season is this dominant, I trust the form over the past, and that is the call.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Second, George Russell. Four wins, consistent podiums, and he knows how to keep pressure on when it matters most for the team.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: His Mexico history is also average sixth, but the car is doing the heavy lifting, and he has been right there all year long.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Third, Lewis Hamilton. Ferrari is strong, he has a Mexico best of second, and he is still a title contender who can change the weekend.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is the hook, one podium in three races there, and he can absolutely hurt when the track suits him and the car is right.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: I'd take Hamilton over Russell if the weather turns, but the data says Mercedes first, so I will go with the data here.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Fair, but Lewis has the track memory, and memory matters at altitude when the air is thin and the laps are long and tricky.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Now, what about Max Verstappen in fourth? He has two wins, and his Mexico history includes a best of first, which is not easy to ignore.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is the quiet warning, Red Bull has been strong, and Max knows how to find the gap late in the race when everyone else is tired.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: And Charles Leclerc in fifth, one win, three podiums, and a best Mexico history that says he can go close again this weekend.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: I like that, he was close to perfect at the last race, and Ferrari has the speed to be in the middle of this all weekend.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Deep cut time, I like Isack Hadjar in eighth, because Red Bull has two wins and he is in top five form, so he can be dangerous.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Why is that a gamble, and can he really match the big names when the pressure is on?

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Because he is not the name everyone is shouting, but a clean lap can put him right in there, and the car is fast enough to make it happen.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Liam Lawson in ninth is the surprise, good points, strong pace, and Racing Bulls can be sneaky under pressure when the track suits them.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Then Pierre Gasly in tenth, most consistent midpack, regular points, and Alpine is just enough to keep him in the mix in the wet.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: So the top three is Kimi, George, and Lewis, with the title hanging in the balance and the weather ready to change everything again.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: The top five is Kimi, George, Lewis, Max, and Charles, so the podium could come from three different teams on race day.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: The rest of the top ten is Norris, Piastri, Hadjar, Lawson, and Gasly, which means the midpack is not just filling space all weekend.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Here is our full top ten, in order, Kimi Antonelli, George Russell, Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc, Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri, Isack Hadjar, Liam Lawson, and Pierre Gasly. Mexico City, let's go, and let's enjoy every lap.
